body: In oxygen-producing photosynthesis, cells use light energy to build organic molecules from carbon dioxide. Water supplies electrons and oxygen is released. Plants, algae and cyanobacteria carry out this process. The chloroplasts visible in the leaf micrograph are sites of photosynthesis in plant cells.

During aerobic cellular respiration, cells transfer energy from organic compounds into forms that can support their work. Oxygen accepts electrons at the end of a series of transfers. Cells of photosynthetic plants also respire. Other metabolic pathways enable living cells to obtain energy when oxygen is unavailable.
credit: Centauri Archive editorial draft, written with AI assistance
limitations: This overview describes familiar pathways. Some forms of photosynthesis do not release oxygen, and the availability and use of light and oxygen vary among environments.
purpose: Trace light capture and cellular energy transfer in paired processes.
